title: How do new plants begin?
summary: Practise how plants reproduce using flowers, fruits and seeds.
keyIdeas: In flowering plants, parts of flowers develop into fruits with seeds.
A seed needs water, air and a suitable temperature to germinate, or start growing.
Insects and wind help carry pollen.

basicKnowledge: A. Cultura científica › La vida en nuestro planeta
A. Cultura científica › Iniciación en la actividad científica

activities.prompt: Where do a tomato plant's seeds begin to form?
activities.explanation: Tomato seeds develop from parts of the flowers.
activities.hint: These parts have pretty coloured petals.

activities.prompt: A fruit protects the seeds inside it.
activities.explanation: A fruit protects its seeds as they develop.

activities.prompt: Match each part to its job in reproduction.
activities.explanation: Each part helps new plants begin.

pairs.right: Can grow into a new plant

activities.prompt: Put a tomato plant's life cycle in order.
activities.explanation: First the seed germinates. Then the plant grows, flowers and produces fruit.
items: A seed falls into damp soil
The seed germinates and a stem appears
The plant grows and has yellow flowers
Parts of the flowers become tomatoes with seeds

activities.prompt: Lucía puts a healthy bean seed in damp cotton wool, with air and a suitable temperature. What could happen?
activities.explanation: A healthy seed with water, air and a suitable temperature can germinate.
activities.hint: Water helps the seed start growing.
options: The seed will become a stone
The seed will germinate and a root will appear

activities.prompt: Sort these seeds by how they travel to new places.
activities.explanation: Wind and animals help spread seeds in nature.

items.text: An acorn hidden by a squirrel
A sweet fruit eaten by a bird

activities.prompt: Hugo thinks flowers are only decorations. Why is he wrong?
activities.explanation: Flowers help flowering plants produce fruits and seeds.
activities.hint: Think about the job of flowers on a tomato plant.
options: They hold the plant in the soil
They drink water from the soil
They allow the plant to reproduce

activities.explanation: Insects carry pollen on their bodies from one flower to another.
activities.sentence: Bees carry ___ from one flower to another.

activities.prompt: Two healthy seeds have air and a suitable temperature. Omar wets his seed; Aisha's stays dry. Which can germinate?
activities.explanation: Seeds need water to germinate. In this comparison, Omar's seed has the water it needs.
activities.hint: Look for the seed that is damp.
options: Both, even though one has no water

activities.prompt: Read the story and answer the questions.
activities.explanation: Fruits protect seeds that can grow into new plants.
activities.title: The apple's secret
activities.text: Aisha walks through the school garden. She finds a fallen red apple. Her teacher shows her the pips inside. They are the apple tree's seeds. Healthy seeds with water, air and a suitable temperature can germinate and grow into a new apple tree.

questions.prompt: What did Aisha find inside the apple?
questions.explanation: The pips inside an apple are its seeds.

questions.prompt: If these seeds germinate, what plant will grow?
questions.explanation: Apple tree seeds can grow into new apple trees.
